summary: A complete target-level planning pass for R23.1–R24.2. Moret–Bailly is developed from incomplete Skolem data through its curve/Picard/approximation proof to split, unramified and algebraic-closure local conditions, soluble prescribed completions, finite-quotient specialisation and the function-field constant-field variant. H6 owns the auxiliary moduli/local objects; R23.2 only chooses and applies them. Residual modularity includes the independent auxiliary-prime lifting input and a totally-real/Snowden/BCGP export. Field control imports R17.4/R17.6 descent. Global finiteness treats KW’s unframed ring and the wider ordinary Thorne/CG input with exact open adapters; characteristic-zero extraction reuses the R03.4 algebra theorem. Every scoped target is accounted for, but sources, supplier interfaces and suggested-signature omissions remain explicitly open. No formalisation or source closure is claimed.

nodes.title: Skolem data, completeness, and integral points (Moret-Bailly II 1.1-1.2, 1.5, 1.8)
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind ring which is either the ring of S-integers of a number field (arithmetic case) or the ring of a smooth connected affine curve over a finite field (geometric case); K = Frac(R), B = Spec R. Let f: X -> B be separated of finite type with f surjective, X_K geometrically irreducible over K, and X irreducible. Let Sigma be a finite set of places of K (archimedean or not) disjoint from Max(R), the closed points of B viewed as places. For v in Sigma fix a finite Galois extension L_v of the completion K_v and a nonempty open subset Omega_v of X(L_v) for the v-topology, consisting of smooth points and stable under Gal(L_v/K_v). The sequence S = (f: X -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) is a Skolem datum; it is complete if every place of K lies in Sigma or in Max(R), and incomplete otherwise. An integral point of S is an irreducible closed subscheme Y of X, finite and surjective over B, such that for every v in Sigma the scheme Y tensor_R L_v is L_v-split (made of L_v-rational points) and contained in Omega_v. Equivalently (Remarque 1.5): Y_K = Spec K' for a finite extension K'/K, the inclusion gives x in X(R') with R' the normalisation of R in K', K' tensor_K L_v is a product of copies of L_v, and every embedding K' -> L_v maps x into Omega_v.
hypotheses: R is the ring of S-integers of a number field or the ring of a smooth connected affine curve over a finite field (Remarque 1.7 extends Théorème 1.3 to any localisation of the ring of integers of a number field or of the ring of a curve over a finite field, by spreading X out)
f separated of finite type and surjective; X irreducible; X_K geometrically irreducible over K
Sigma finite and disjoint from Max(R); each L_v/K_v finite Galois; each Omega_v nonempty, v-adically open, made of smooth points and Gal(L_v/K_v)-stable
incompleteness (some place of K outside Sigma and outside Max(R)) is essential: Remarque 1.8 gives a complete datum without integral point
proofSteps: 1.1 and Définition 1.2 fix the data and the notion of integral point; the displayed local conditions (Sigma, Omega_v, L_v-split) were read on the page image of p. 181 because the OCR drops Sigma and Omega.

Remarque 1.5 reads an integral point as a finite extension K'/K which becomes split after base change to each L_v, together with an R'-integral point of X lying in Omega_v at every embedding K' -> L_v; it notes that this generalises the Cantor-Roquette density theorem (essentially X_K unirational and L_v = K_v).
Remarque 1.8: R = Z, X = G_m over Z, Sigma = {ordinary absolute value}, L = C, Omega = {|z| < 1} is a complete Skolem datum without integral point; the source only says this is immediate.

nodes.title: Density of separable and algebraic points in local point sets (Lemme 1.6.1, Corollaire 1.6.2, Lemme 2.1)
nodes.statement: (Lemme 1.6.1) Let F be a local field, F-bar an algebraic closure, F^s the separable closure of F in F-bar, and X an F-scheme of finite type which is generically smooth over F. Then X(F^s) is dense in X(F-bar) for the valuation topology. (Corollaire 1.6.2) Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers A and let 𝔛 be an A-scheme of finite type, flat and surjective over A, whose generic fibre is generically smooth over F. Then there is a finite separable extension F'/F with ring of integers A' such that 𝔛(A') is nonempty. (Lemme 2.1) Let F be a field with a discrete valuation v, F-hat its completion and F' the algebraic closure of F in F-hat, and assume F-hat is separable over F (i.e. the valuation ring is excellent). Then for every F-scheme Z of finite type, Z(F') is dense in Z(F-hat) for the v-topology.
hypotheses: Lemme 1.6.1: F a local field; X of finite type and generically smooth over F; in characteristic 0 the statement is empty
Corollaire 1.6.2: F non-archimedean; 𝔛 flat and surjective over A; generic fibre generically smooth
Lemme 2.1: F-hat separable over F (excellent valuation ring); the author states he does not know whether this hypothesis is superfluous
proofSteps: 1.6.1(a), X = affine line, char F = p > 0: for x in F-bar with v(x) >= 0 pick k with x^(p^k) = a in F^s; for n >= 1 let y_n be a root of y^(p^k) - t^n y - a = 0 with t a uniformiser of F; then y_n is in F^s, v(y_n) >= 0 and v(y_n - x) = p^(-k) v(y_n^(p^k) - a) = p^(-k) v(t^n y_n) >= n p^(-k) (display read on the page image of p. 183).

1.6.1(b), general case: reduce to X smooth; near the closed point P under x choose a Zariski open U and an F-morphism U -> A^n (n = dim X) finite étale over a neighbourhood of the image of P; it induces a homeomorphism of a neighbourhood of x onto an open of F-bar^n, and a point is F^s-rational iff its image is, because the map is étale; conclude by (a).
1.6.2: with A^s, A-bar the integers of F^s, F-bar, one has 𝔛(A^s) = 𝔛(A-bar) ∩ 𝔛(F^s), and 𝔛(A-bar) is a nonempty open of 𝔛(F-bar) because 𝔛 is flat and surjective over A; apply 1.6.1.

2.1: clear for affine space; in general stratify Z into regular locally closed pieces, note that an F-hat-point factors through the smooth locus, shrink to an étale map Z -> U with U open in affine space, take an F'-point of the (open) image of a given open set and use that fibres of the quasi-finite map consist of points algebraic over F.

nodes.title: Elementary reductions: quasi-projective, shrinking X_K, enlarging Sigma (Remarques 1.4, 1.9, 1.10, Exemple 1.10.1)
nodes.statement: To prove Théorème 1.3 one may assume: (1.4) f quasi-projective, by Chow's lemma (EGA II 5.6); (1.9) X_K smooth: if F_K is a strict closed subset of X_K with closure F in X, then F contains no fibre of f (the closed fibres of f are purely of codimension 1), X - F -> B is still surjective, F(L_v) does not contain Omega_v (the latter is an L_v-analytic manifold of dimension dim X_K > dim F_K), and (X - F -> B, {L_v}, {Omega_v - F(L_v)}) is again a Skolem datum; (1.10) Sigma may be enlarged by a finite set S of closed points of B: B_1 = B - S is affine because Pic(B) = Cl(R) is finite, for v in S Corollaire 1.6.2 gives a finite Galois L_v/K_v with integers R'_v such that Omega_v := X(R'_v) is a nonempty Galois-stable open of X(L_v), the datum S_1 = (X_1 = X x_B B_1 -> B_1, Sigma ∪ S, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) is a Skolem datum, and the closure in X of an integral point of S_1 is an integral point of S. (1.10.1) Consequently X may be replaced by any nonempty open subscheme, e.g. X smooth over B.

nodes.statement: Assume f quasi-projective and X_K smooth. (Lemme 2.3) If dim X_K = n >= 2, there is a hypersurface X'_K of X_K, geometrically irreducible, containing T_K and regular at the points of T_K. (2.4) With X' the closure of X'_K in X and Omega'_v = {smooth points of X'_K(L_v)} ∩ Omega_v, the datum S' = (X' -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega'_v}) is a Skolem datum, incomplete if S is, with dim X'_K = dim X_K - 1, and the image in X of an integral point of S' is an integral point of S. nodes.title: Curve case set-up: generalized Picard functor PG(X̄, Z) and the affine-space fibration of effective divisors (3.1-3.6)
nodes.statement: Let S = (f: X -> B, Sigma, {L_v}, {Omega_v}) be a Skolem datum with dim X_K = 1 and f quasi-projective and smooth. Choose a compactification j: X -> X-bar over B with f-bar projective and X-bar normal; Z = X-bar - X with its reduced structure; g = h^1(X-bar_K, O) and z = deg_K(Z_K), with z > 0 after enlarging Z. After shrinking B and enlarging Sigma (1.10): (3.1.2) X-bar is regular, the fibres of f-bar are geometrically integral, and Z is regular and finite, flat and surjective over B (so a Cartier divisor). For d in N the symmetric power X^(d) = X^d/S_d (fibre product over B) represents effective Cartier divisors of X-bar_S finite flat of degree d over S and disjoint from Z; U_d ⊂ X^(d) is the open of étale divisors; Omega_v^[d] ⊂ U_d(K_v) is the set of effective étale divisors of degree d on X ⊗ K_v which are L_v-split and contained in Omega_v. PG(X-bar, Z)(S) (resp. PG_d) is the group of isomorphism classes of pairs (line bundle L on X-bar_S, trivialisation of L on Z_S) (resp. with L of degree d); there is an exact sequence of sheaves 1 -> G_m,B -> (pi_Z)_* G_m,Z -> PG(X-bar, Z) -> Pic_{X-bar/B} -> 1, and PG(X-bar, Z) is represented by a smooth separated group scheme locally of finite presentation (only the representability of its generic fibre, from Murre's theorem, SGA 6 XII 1.5, is used). The map phi_d: X^(d) -> PG_d, D -> cl^Z(D) = class of (O(D), s_D restricted to Z), has fibres described by (3.5.4). Lemme 3.3: Omega_v^[d] is open in U_d(K_v) for all d >= 0, and nonempty if [L_v : K_v] divides d. Lemme 3.6: if d >= 2g + z - 1, phi_d is a locally trivial fibration in affine spaces of dimension d + 1 - g - z.
hypotheses: dim X_K = 1, f quasi-projective and smooth (reached by 1.4, 1.9, 1.10 and section 2)
normalisation of X-bar keeps X unchanged because X is regular (f smooth)
(3.1.2) is achieved only after replacing B by an open subscheme and enlarging Sigma; it cites EGA IV 12.2.1 for geometric integrality of fibres
the inequality in Lemme 3.6 is d >= 2g + z - 1 (checked on page image p. 189; the OCR prints it garbled)
the duality argument of 3.6 uses that X-bar is regular hence Gorenstein and that each fibre X-bar_b is geometrically reduced
proofSteps: 3.2: the projection X^d -> X^(d) is étale off the diagonals; (3.2.3) identifies X^(d)(S) with effective Cartier divisors finite flat of degree d over S and disjoint from Z (X smooth over B).

Lemme 3.3(i): Omega_v^[d] = Omega' ∩ U_d(K_v) where Omega' is the image of Omega_v^d minus diagonals under an étale projection, hence open. (ii): with delta = [L_v : K_v] and d = r delta, the union of the proper intermediate analytic submanifolds Omega_v ∩ X(M) has empty interior, so there are r points of degree delta over K_v, pairwise non-conjugate, whose conjugates form a K_v-rational divisor in Omega_v^[d].

3.4: rigidity of the categories of pairs (from 3.1.2(ii) and surjectivity of Z -> B) makes PG sheaves; (3.4.2) exhibits PG(X-bar, Z) as an extension of Pic by the smooth affine group (pi_Z)_* G_m,Z / G_m,B.
3.5: a section s of L with s|Z = alpha is regular, and div(s) is in X^(d)(S); this gives the bijection (3.5.4) between X^(d)(S) and triples (L, alpha, s).

Lemme 3.6: for d >= 2g + z - 1, R^1 pr_2* of the universal bundle and of its twist by -Z vanish by duality; so the direct images E_d, N_d commute with base change and the restriction r_d: E_d -> F_d is a surjection of locally free sheaves with kernel N_d; the subscheme r_d^(-1)(Im sigma_d) of V(E_d-dual) is U^(d)... identified with X^(d) over P_d, a torsor under the vector bundle V(N_d-dual) of rank d + 1 - g - z.

nodes.statement: Keep the curve set-up (3.1.2), P_d = PG_d(X-bar, Z), and put W_v^[d] = phi_d(Omega_v^[d]) ⊂ P_d(K_v) for v in Sigma. (Lemme 3.7.2) (i) For d >= 2g + z - 1, W_v^[d] is open in P_d(K_v), and nonempty if d is a multiple of [L_v : K_v]. (ii) For d, d' >= 0 with d >= 2g + z, W_v^[d] · W_v^[d'] ⊂ W_v^[d+d'] in the group PG(X-bar, Z). nodes.statement: (Lemme 3.9) Let M_0 be an ample invertible sheaf on X-bar (deg(M_0)_K > 0). If S is incomplete there are n >= 1 and a trivialisation alpha of M_0^{⊗n}|Z such that (M_0^{⊗n}, alpha) satisfies the hypotheses of Lemme 3.8. nodes.title: Taylor's Theorem G: points over the maximal extension split at S are Zariski dense
nodes.statement: (Taylor, Theorem G, attributed to Moret-Bailly [M] = part II) Let K be a number field and S a finite set of places of K; let K_S be the unique maximal extension of K inside a fixed algebraic closure in which all places of S split completely (for K = Q and S = {infinity}, K_S is the maximal totally real field). If X/Spec K is a geometrically irreducible smooth quasi-projective scheme with X(K_v) nonempty for all v in S, then X(K_S) is Zariski dense in X. KW II (proof of Theorem 6.1) uses the stronger form with open sets: applying Théorème 1.3 with prescribed v-adic open subsets Omega_v of local points (for example the points of X(Q_p) reducing to a given integral point x_v) yields a point over a field split at the given places whose local images lie in Omega_v.
hypotheses: K a number field; S finite; X geometrically irreducible, smooth and quasi-projective over K; X(K_v) nonempty for every v in S
the conclusion concerns K_S, an infinite extension; a single point lies over a finite subextension K' ⊂ K_S, which need not be Galois over K
proofSteps: Taylor recalls Theorem G in the introduction and applies it in section 1 with S = places above l, p and infinity; no proof is given in Taylor.

Intended deduction (not written in the sources read): let S' be a finite set of places of K containing S, the archimedean places, one finite place v_0 not in S and the places of bad behaviour of a chosen model; let R be the ring of S'-integers and spread X out to an irreducible separated finite-type R-scheme, surjective over Spec R after enlarging S'; put Sigma = S, which is disjoint from Max(R) and leaves v_0 outside Sigma ∪ Max(R) (incomplete datum); take L_v = K_v and Omega_v = X(K_v) ∩ U(K_v) for a nonempty Zariski open U of X_K (nonempty by the analytic-dimension argument of Remarque 1.9, since X is smooth and X(K_v) is nonempty); Théorème 1.3 and Remarque 1.5 give K' with K' ⊗_K K_v a product of copies of K_v for v in S, i.e. K' ⊂ K_S, and a point of U(K').
Real places: for v real in S and L_v = R, splitting completely means every embedding of K' extending v is real; this is how Taylor obtains totally real fields.

nodes.title: Forcing linear disjointness from a given finite extension by extra split places
nodes.statement: Let D/K be finite Galois over a global field. Choose extra unramified places outside a finite forbidden set where the smooth geometrically connected variety has local points, with Frobenii generating Gal(D/K), or one nonsplit place for each simple Galois subextension D_i/K. Every finite Galois K′/K split at these places is linearly disjoint from D/K. The Galois hypothesis on K′ is used: K′∩D is a normal intermediate field. Its Frobenii are trivial at all the chosen split places, hence it equals K. For a non-Galois avoidance extension use its normal closure.

nodes.title: KW II Theorem 6.1 (i)-(ii): potential modularity of rho-bar of S-type over a totally real Galois F of even degree, in weight k(rho-bar) and in weight 2
nodes.statement: Let rho-bar: G_Q -> GL_2(F) be of S-type (odd, absolutely irreducible) with 2 <= k(rho-bar) <= p + 1 if p > 2; assume rho-bar has non-solvable image if p = 2, and rho-bar|Q(mu_p) absolutely irreducible if p > 2. Then there is a totally real field F, Galois over Q of even degree, unramified at p, and even split above p if rho-bar|D_p is irreducible, with im(rho-bar) = im(rho-bar|G_F) and rho-bar|F(mu_p) absolutely irreducible, such that: (i) assuming k(rho-bar) = 2 if p = 2, rho-bar|G_F arises from a cuspidal automorphic representation pi of GL_2(A_F) that is discrete series of weight k(rho-bar) at the infinite places and unramified at all places above p; (ii) rho-bar|G_F also arises from a cuspidal pi with pi_v of conductor dividing v at all v | p (and unramified if rho-bar is finite flat at v) and of weight 2 at the infinite places. Part (iii) (control of F) is recorded under R23.5.
hypotheses: S-type; 2 <= k(rho-bar) <= p + 1 for p > 2; non-solvable image for p = 2; rho-bar|Q(mu_p) absolutely irreducible for p > 2
part (i) at p = 2 is only claimed for k(rho-bar) = 2

the proof supplements Taylor 2002 [58], Taylor 2006 [59] and Theorem 2.1 of Khare [33] (level-one paper; the library copy is arXiv v1 whose numbering differs) with the arguments printed in italics; it does not use any characteristic-zero lift of rho-bar

imports: Langlands-Tunnell [40], [65]; Gross [27] Theorem 13.10 and Propositions 8.13, 8.18; Coleman-Voloch [12]; KW II Theorem 8.2; CDT appendix B; Hida [30] section 8; Lemma 2.2 of [33]; Grunwald-Wang

Snowden’s general totally real theorem is a separate weight-two export; the precise Serre weight, even degree and dyadic assertions here still require the original KW/Taylor refinements and cannot be obtained by simply setting F=Q in Snowden.
proofSteps: Apply modularity lifting first to the auxiliary Tate representation of the H6 abelian variety, not to a lift of the original residual representation. Use R19.2 to state modularity, R22.5/R22.6 or the corrected totally real ordinary input, R20.3 for the solvable-image weights, R22.4 for KW II Theorem 8.2 and L5 for the ordinary weight adjustment; Khare Lemma 2.2 comes from R18.3.

Dihedral projective image: choose all auxiliary fields linearly disjoint from the field cut out by rho-bar and split at a prime split in the projective kernel field but inert in the quadratic subfield of Q(mu_p); this keeps rho-bar|G_F(mu_p) irreducible.

Solvable image: Langlands-Tunnell give rho-bar from S_k(Gamma_1(N)) with k >= 2; Gross Theorem 13.10, Coleman-Voloch and Gross Propositions 8.13, 8.18 give weight k(rho-bar) with N prime to p and also S_2(Gamma_1(Np)); so (alpha), (beta) of 8.2 hold and Theorem 8.2 gives (i), (ii).

Non-solvable image: Taylor's moduli problem X for HBAVs (field M, embedding i, polarisation datum j, level structure alpha at lambda | p and at auxiliary primes p_0 ([58]) or p_1, p_2 ([59])); a point of X over F from Moret-Bailly using local points at infinity, p and the auxiliary primes; modularity of V_wp(A) (or of B from Lemma 4.4 of [59]) gives modularity of rho-bar|G_F.
p = 2 real points: construction from Taylor's erratum ([59] p. 776), with the modified lattice L' when rho-bar(c) is non-trivial (see the R23.2 local-points node).
p = 2, k(rho-bar) = 4: choose A with completely toric reduction above 2 (first case of Lemma 1.2 of [58]) to get pi of weight 2 and level v above 2.

k(rho-bar) = 2: if rho-bar|D_p irreducible, impose chi unramified at p in Lemma 4.3 of [59], so Proposition 4.1(3) of [59] gives an unramified Weil-Deligne parameter; if rho-bar is ordinary, twist so det(rho-bar) chi_p^{-1}|D_p is trivial, use Taylor's lifting chi~_v with Frobenius beta_v and F~_v = Q_p, lift the extension class x to x_lambda in H^1(D_v, O_{M,lambda}(chi_p chi~_v^{-2})) (the obstruction in H^2 vanishes: no obstruction if chi_v^2 ≠ 1; if chi_v^2 = 1 compare with the Kummer obstruction o_0 = 0 and identify o with the cup product of an unramified eta with the finite class x), obtaining A_v with good ordinary reduction and an integral point x_v in X(Z_p) (normalised integral model), then apply Moret-Bailly Théorème 1.3 of part II with Omega_v = points of X(Q_p) reducing to x_v.
p = 3 with rho-bar|D_p irreducible: section 5 of [59] excludes p = 3; Lemma 2.2 of [33] lifts this (unread).

p ≠ 2, rho-bar|D_p reducible, k(rho-bar) > 2: the proof of Lemma 1.5 of [58] shows A ordinary at v with inertial Weil-Deligne parameter (omega^{k(rho-bar)-2} ⊕ 1, 0) if k ≠ p+1 and (1 ⊕ 1, N), N ≠ 0 nilpotent, if k = p+1 (for k = p with rho-bar|D_p semisimple it gives (omega^{-1} ⊕ 1, 0) without saying which line lifts the cyclotomic line); with CDT appendix B this gives pi of parallel weight 2 ordinary with the same inertial parameter, and Hida theory ([30] section 8, with Lemma 2.2 of [33] for neatness) gives pi unramified above p of parallel weight k(rho-bar).

nodes.title: KW II Theorem 10.1: R̄_S^psi is finite over Z_p, by restriction to the auxiliary totally real field
nodes.statement: For rho-bar, S, psi and local conditions as in 10.1, the ring R̄_S^psi is finite as a Z_p-module.
hypotheses: all hypotheses of 10.1 (S-type, weight range, non-solvable image for p = 2, rho-bar|Q(mu_p) absolutely irreducible for p > 2, local conditions from Theorem 3.1, case (C) at p > 2 only for k(rho-bar) = p + 1)

inputs: Theorem 6.1 and Theorem 8.2 (through the auxiliary field F), Propositions 9.2 and 9.3 (R = T and finiteness over F), and the finite-image criterion 'Lemma 3.6 of [34]' = KW Annals Lemma 3.6 or '3.14 of [31]' = de Jong

the ring over F, R̄_F^{psi_F}, parametrises minimal odd deformations of rho-bar_F unramified outside the places above p with determinant psi_F chi_p and uniformly one of the conditions (A), (B), (C) at all places above p

the rings are those of GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.6 (framed ring over the local conditions of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6; the unframed R̄^ψ_S as trace subring); only the unframed ring is finite: the framed ring is a power series ring over it in 4|S| − 1 variables
proofSteps: Choose F as in the previous node and let R̄_F^{psi_F} be the ring over F described in the hypotheses; the representation rho_{pi'} prescribes lifting data (pi' chosen according to the type (A), (B) or (C)).
Apply Propositions 9.2 (p > 2) and 9.3 (p = 2) to R̄_F^{psi_F}: it is finite as a Z_p-module.

Functoriality (rho-bar and rho-bar|G_F absolutely irreducible) gives CNL_O-morphisms pi_1: R_F^{psi_F} -> R̄_F^{psi_F}, pi_2: R_{Q,S}^psi -> R̄_{Q,S}^psi, beta: R_F^{psi_F} -> R_{Q,S}^psi (restriction to G_F, using condition (4) and the compatibility of the local conditions at p) and alpha on the framed quotients, with alpha pi_1 = pi_2 beta; hence beta induces gamma: R̄_F^{psi_F} -> R̄_{Q,S}^psi.

gamma carries the universal mod p representation of G_F over R̄_F^{psi_F}/(p), which has finite image because R̄_F^{psi_F} is finite, to the restriction to G_F of the universal mod p representation of G_Q over R̄_{Q,S}^psi/(p); so the latter has finite image on G_F, hence on G_Q.
The finite-image criterion (KW Annals Lemma 3.6, or de Jong 3.14) gives R̄_S^psi finite over Z_p.

nodes.title: Existence of characteristic-zero points of R̄_S^psi and of the associated lifts of the required local type
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of 10.1, abs.dim R̄_S^psi >= 1 (Proposition 4.5) and R̄_S^psi is finite over Z_p (Theorem 10.1). Hence (Corollary 4.7) there is a local O-algebra map R̄_S^psi -> O' with O' the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p, and, since R̄_{S,psi}^□ is formally smooth over R̄_S^psi, a map R̄_{S,psi}^□ -> O''. The corresponding tuple gives a continuous representation rho: G_Q -> GL_2(O'') reducing to rho-bar, with det rho = psi chi_p, unramified outside S, whose restriction to D_v (after conjugation by the framing g_v ∈ GL_2(O'')^1) is a lift classified by R̄_{v,psi}^□ for every v in S; that is, rho is a p-adic lift of the required type (KW II 10.3.1).
hypotheses: finiteness of the unframed R̄_S^psi over Z_p (R24.1); the framed ring is not finite over O

the dimension lower bound requires the local rings to be flat of the stated dimensions (previous node) and the relation bound r(J) <= dim H^1_{L⊥}(S, (Ad^0)*(1)) of Lemma 4.6 together with the generator count g = dim H^1_{L⊥}(S, (Ad^0)*(1)) + |S| - 1 (Lemma 4.4, Wiles' formula, Lemma 4.3)
finiteness alone is insufficient: a finite O-algebra of dimension 0 (e.g. F, or O/pi^n[x]/(x^2)) has no characteristic-zero point; it is the bound abs.dim >= 1 that makes p non-nilpotent
that O'-points of R̄_{v,psi}^□ are exactly lifts of type X_v is the 'classifies' property of Definition 2.4 / Corollary 2.3 for the flat reduced local quotients
continuity and reduction to rho-bar are immediate from the construction of universal lifts over complete local rings and are not argued separately in the source
proofSteps: Presentation: R_{S,psi}^□ ≅ R_{S,loc,psi}^□[[X_1, ..., X_g]]/J with g = dim H^1_{L⊥}(S, (Ad^0)*(1)) + |S| - 1 (Lemma 4.4, Wiles' formula (2), Lemma 4.3(3), and the exact sequence 0 -> H^0(D_v, Ad^0) -> H^0(D_v, Ad) -> F -> L_v -> 0 making each local term 1).
Relations: J needs at most dim H^1_{L⊥}(S, (Ad^0)*(1)) generators (Lemma 4.6); base change gives R̄_{S,psi}^□ ≅ R̄_{S,loc,psi}^□[[X_1, ..., X_g]]/J' with the same bound.
Dimension: abs.dim R̄_{S,psi}^□ >= |S| - 1 + (1 + 3|S|) = 4|S|, while abs.dim R̄_{S,psi}^□ = abs.dim R̄_S^psi + 4|S| - 1 (Proposition 4.1); so abs.dim R̄_S^psi >= 1 (Proposition 4.5).
Corollary 4.7: finite over Z_p and dimension >= 1 force p non-nilpotent, so a prime I with p ∉ I exists and R̄_S^psi/I embeds in some O'; lift to the framed ring by formal smoothness.
10.3.1: the O''-points of R̄_{S,psi}^□ correspond to p-adic lifts of the required type, so a lift of that type exists as soon as R̄_S^psi is finite, which is Theorem 10.1.

nodes.title: Deducing Taylor's Theorem G from Moret-Bailly's Théorème 1.3
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places and X/K geometrically irreducible, smooth and quasi-projective with X(K_v) ≠ ∅ for v ∈ S. For every nonempty Zariski open U ⊆ X there is a finite K′/K inside K_S with U(K′) ≠ ∅; hence X(K_S) is Zariski dense. Deduction: spread U out to an irreducible, surjective, separated finite-type model 𝒰 over R = 𝒪_K[1/N], with N chosen so that some finite place w ∉ S divides N and is omitted from Σ = S; take L_v = K_v and Ω_v = U(K_v)^{sm} ≠ ∅ (U is dense in the smooth X and X(K_v) ≠ ∅); the Skolem datum is incomplete (w ∉ Σ ∪ Max(R)); Théorème 1.3 gives an integral point, i.e. a point of U over K′ split completely at every v ∈ S (Remarque 1.5), so K′ ⊆ K_S.

proofSteps: Spread out U over O_K[1/N], invert every finite place of S and one additional finite place w outside S. The extra inverted place w is absent from both Σ=S and Max(R), so the datum is incomplete.
Local data: L_v = K_v, Ω_v = U(K_v)^{sm}, open and nonempty.
Apply Théorème 1.3 and Remarque 1.5.

nodes.title: Taylor's auxiliary data for the ordinary-at-l case: the prime p, the CM extension L/F, the character psi, and the fields N and M
nodes.statement: Standing hypotheses of Taylor 2002 section 1 as corrected in Taylor 2006 (pp. 776-777): l an odd prime, k/F_l finite, F totally real, rho-bar: G_F -> GL_2(k) continuous with insoluble image, rho-bar|G_v ~ (epsilon chi_v^{-1}, *; 0, chi_v) for every place v of F above l, and det rho-bar = epsilon (the corrected third bullet; epsilon the l-adic cyclotomic character mod l). For v | l let F~_v be the smallest totally tamely ramified extension of F_v over which chi_v becomes unramified. Let zeta be a primitive #k^× root of unity and N_0 = Q(zeta, sqrt(1-4l)); l is unramified in N_0 and every prime of N_0 above l has residue field isomorphic to k; fix lambda_0 | l and O_{N_0}/lambda_0 ≅ k. For v | l put beta_v = zeta^{b_v} ((1+sqrt(1-4l))/2)^{[k(v):F_l]} with beta_v ≡ chi_v(phi_v) mod lambda_0 for a Frobenius lift phi_v in G_{F~_v}, and let chi~_v: W_{F_v} -> N_0^× be the unique character which, if chi_v^2 ≠ 1, sends phi_v to beta_v and is the Teichmüller lift of chi_v on inertia, and, if chi_v^2 = 1, is the Teichmüller lift of chi_v. Choose an odd prime p ≠ l such that: rho-bar is unramified at all w | p with rho-bar(Frob_w) having distinct eigenvalues; p splits completely in the Hilbert class field of N_0; p splits completely in the fixed field of ker(epsilon^{-1} det rho-bar); p is coprime to beta_v - beta_v^c for all v | l. Choose wp_0 | p in N_0, and for w | p choose alpha'_w in Z[(1+sqrt(1-4l))/2] of norm p and alpha_w = zeta^{a_w} alpha'_w congruent to an eigenvalue of rho-bar(Frob_w). By Lemma 1.1 choose a quadratic L/F and psi: G_L -> (N-bar_{0,wp_0})^× with: L totally imaginary and not contained in F(zeta_p); each v | l splits as v_1 v_1^c in L with psi|W_{L_{v_1}} = chi~_v in (O_{N_0}/wp_0)^ac; each w | p splits as w_1 w_1^c with psi|G_{w_1} unramified sending arithmetic Frobenius to a lift of alpha_w; det Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} psi = epsilon_p. Then psi-bar|G_{v_1} ≠ psi-bar^c|G_{v_1} for v | l. Finally choose a Galois CM extension N/N_0 in which primes above l split, primes above p are unramified, and some wp | wp_0 has psi-bar valued in O_N/wp; choose lambda | lambda_0 in O_N and let M be the maximal totally real subfield of N.

nodes.title: Taylor Lemma 1.1: a character of a CM quadratic extension with prescribed local reductions and prescribed determinant of its induction
nodes.statement: Let p be a rational prime, O the integers of a finite extension of Q_p with residue field F. Let K be totally real and L/K a totally imaginary quadratic extension in which every place of K above p splits. Let S be a finite set of finite places of K which split in L and contain all places above p, and S_L a set of places of L containing exactly one place above each element of S. Let phi: G_K -> O^× be continuous, sending every complex conjugation to -1 and of the form epsilon_p^n times a finite-order character for some n in Z. For each x in S_L let psi-bar_x: G_{L_x} -> F^× be continuous. Then there are a finite extension of Frac(O), with integers O' and residue field k', and a continuous character psi: G_L -> (O')^× such that for all x in S_L, psi|G_{L_x} is finitely ramified and reduces to psi-bar_x, and det Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} psi = phi.
hypotheses: every place of K above p splits in L; every place of S splits in L; S contains the places above p
phi odd (every complex conjugation to -1) and a power of epsilon_p times a finite-order character
the final step imports 'lemma 2.1 of [Ta2]' (Taylor, On icosahedral Artin representations II, Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003)), which the source calls presumably well known; [Ta2] was not read
the proof's second displayed condition reads 'coincides with ψ_x on L_y^× for y ∈ S_L'; ψ_y is meant (source issue PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems/E5)
proofSteps: Choose psi_0 with epsilon_p^{-1} det Ind psi_0 of finite order and psi_0|I_x of finite order for x in S_L; seeking psi = psi_0^n psi' reduces to n = 0; one may assume S_L generates the class group of L.

By class field theory, let psi_x: L_x^× -> O^× correspond to the Teichmüller lift of psi-bar_x and phi' the idele character of K attached to phi times the quadratic character of L/K; one must find psi: A_L^×/L^× -> (O')^× restricting to phi' on A_K^× and to psi_x on L_x^× for x in S_L.

With T the finite places outside S where phi' ramifies and chosen extensions psi_x of phi'|O_{K,x}^× to O_{L,x}^× for x in T, define psi_0 on (prod_{x in S} L_x^× × prod_{x in T} O_{L,x}^×)/K_S^×; it suffices to extend to a character of the product with prod_{y not in S∪T} (O_{L,y}^×/O_{K,y}^×) modulo L_S^×, i.e. to find a continuous character on that last product agreeing with psi_0 on L_S^×/K_S^×.

As psi_0 has finite order it suffices that every finite-index subgroup of L_S^×/K_S^× contains the preimage of an open subgroup of prod_{y not in S∪T} O_{L,y}^×/O_{K,y}^×; the commutative diagram with the map c-1 and finite generation of L_S^× reduce this to: for every n, (L_S^×)^n contains the preimage of an open subgroup of prod O_{L,y}^× -- the imported statement from [Ta2], Lemma 2.1.

nodes.statement: Let v be an unramified place of F above l and x a place of E above v. Suppose chi_v^2|I_v = epsilon^n|I_v for some integer n with 0 <= n < l - 1, and suppose that n ≠ 1 if rho-bar|G_v is semisimple. In the good reduction case, over W(k(x)^ac)[zeta_l] the only simple subquotients of the finite flat group scheme A[lambda] are Z/lZ and mu_l, and there are no nontrivial extensions of Z/lZ by Z/lZ nor of mu_l by mu_l; with the connected-étale sequence and dim Lie(A[lambda] × F_l^ac) = [O_N/lambda : F_l] this gives 0 -> mu_l^[O_N/lambda:F_l] -> A[lambda] -> (Z/lZ)^[O_N/lambda:F_l] -> 0, so A has ordinary reduction; done if rho-bar|G_v is not semisimple.

nodes.statement: For the M-HBAV A/E of the Moret-Bailly application: (a) (Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} psi-bar)|G_E is absolutely irreducible, since for every place x of E above p the restrictions of psi-bar to the two places of LE above x are different; (b) A has semistable reduction at every prime x of E above p, because A[lambda] is unramified at x and ker(GL_2(O_{M,lambda}) -> GL_2(O_M/lambda)) has no nontrivial element of finite order; (c) T_wp A is ordinary at every x above p, because A is semistable at x, E_x ≅ Q_p and the I_x-coinvariants of A[wp] are nontrivial; (d) since (Ind psi)|G_E is modular, Theorem 5.1 of Skinner-Wiles [SW3] (nearly ordinary deformations of irreducible residual representations) shows that T_wp A is modular, hence T_lambda A is modular; consequently rho-bar|G_E ≅ A[lambda] is the reduction of a modular lambda-adic representation.

nodes.title: Taylor Theorem 1.6 (with the 2006 corrected proof) and Corollary 1.7: potential modularity of residual representations
nodes.statement: (Theorem 1.6) Let l be an odd prime, k/F_l finite, F totally real and rho-bar: G_F -> GL_2(k) continuous irreducible with rho-bar|G_v ~ (epsilon chi_v^{-1}, *; 0, chi_v) for every v | l and det rho-bar(c) = -1 for every complex conjugation c. Moreover E, pi, lambda' may be chosen so that for every unramified prime x of E above l with chi_x^2|I_x = epsilon^n|I_x and rho-bar(I_x) not consisting of scalar matrices, rho_{pi,lambda'}|G_x ~ (epsilon (chi'_x)^{-1}, *; 0, chi'_x) with chi'_x a tamely ramified lift of chi_x. (Corollary 1.7) Without the local hypothesis at l: if rho-bar is continuous irreducible and odd, there are a finite Galois totally real E/F in which every prime of F above l is unramified with inertial degree at most 2, pi and lambda' with rho-bar_{pi,lambda'} ~ rho-bar|G_E, with a corresponding ordinarity refinement at the set T of unramified v | l where rho-bar(I_v) is not scalar and rho-bar|G_v is reducible of the displayed shape.

nodes.title: Taylor 2006 Lemma 1.3: definite quaternionic forms, cuspidal representations and their Galois representations
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of even degree, D the quaternion algebra over F ramified exactly at the infinite places, (k⃗, w⃗) a weight with k_σ ≥ 2 and w = k_σ − 1 + 2w_σ independent of σ, and ψ : 𝔸_F^×/F^× → (ℚ̄_l)^× continuous with ψ(a) = (Na)^{1−w} on an open subgroup of F_l^×. (Lemma 1.3.) (1) S_{(k⃗,w⃗),ℚ̄_l,ψ}(U_l) is a semisimple admissible representation of GL₂(𝔸_F^{∞,l}) with U^l-invariants S_{(k⃗,w⃗),ℚ̄_l,ψ}(U_l × U^l); (2) after ⊗_{ℚ̄_l,i} ℂ its quotient by the 'triv' subspace (functions factoring through the reduced norm, nonzero only in parallel weight 2) is ⊕_π π^{∞,l} ⊗ π_l^{U_l} over regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL₂(𝔸_F) of weight (k⃗, w⃗) and central character ψ_i; (3)–(4) the same at weight 2 over all U, with the one-dimensional characters χ, χ² = ψ, added. nodes.title: Generating Frobenius primes
nodes.statement: Let D/K be finite Galois over a global field and B a finite set of places. There is a finite set T of unramified places outside B and choices of primes of D above them whose Frobenius elements generate Gal(D/K). In particular, for every nontrivial simple Galois intermediate D_i/K one can choose a place outside B not split in D_i. For a function field one uses its arithmetic Chebotarev theorem, including the restrictions imposed by the constant field.
hypotheses: All hypotheses in the statement are required; the supplier interfaces below are not claims of implementation.
